decided: clampFraction maps NaN to 0 (no recovery assumed) via an explicit math.IsNaN guard; +/-Inf already resolve through the existing comparisons (-Inf < 0 -> 0, +Inf > 1 -> 1). The doc comment is corrected to state the NaN rule. No signature change, no error return.
why: clampFraction is the last money-path bound that lets NaN through (workspace-hmt swept the rest). Recovery scales loss by (1-recovery), so the conservative failure mode for a garbage fraction is 'assume nothing recovers' — report the full loss — which is 0, the same end of the range a negative misconfiguration maps to. Returning an error instead would change the signature for a case registry.Parse already rejects (non-finite fractions cannot reach these call sites today); this is defence-in-depth, and defence-in-depth should not tax every caller.
cost_if_wrong: If NaN->0 is the wrong choice, an unrealized-loss figure computed from a hypothetically NaN recovery is overstated by the recovery fraction rather than corrupted. The alternative cost we are eliminating: int64(NaN) is architecture-dependent (0 on arm64, math.MinInt64 on amd64) — silent, platform-divergent money corruption in a repo whose goldens depend on cross-arch determinism.
alternatives: NaN -> 1: erases the loss entirely (reports zero unrealized value) — the exact outcome the comment promises cannot happen; rejected.
Return an error / panic: forces both call sites and future callers to handle an unreachable case; registry.Parse (workspace-hmt) already owns input validation; rejected as the wrong layer.
Do nothing (unreachable today): leaves a false doc comment on a HIGH-tier money path and an arch-dependent int64(NaN) conversion one refactor away; rejected per the bead.
scope: engine/unrealized.go clampFraction only; no call-site or signature changes.
